questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I was important to me that I new the language. I also wanted it to be a place with a good study environment and outgoing people. Lastly, I've just always really wanted to live in the UK for a bit, and this seemed like a great opportunity.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it to be a bit difficult, but it all worked out.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I used my flatmates, who were also on exchange like me. And also, the university provided a personal tutor, who I had a zoom call with in the beginning to make sure I knew everything. She was available to me throughout my entire stay.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I was a bit difficult, but I just went on a lot of different Facebook-groups and wrote to people. I ended up living with two other exchange students, who had found an Airbnb, which we could rent for four months.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I don't know. I quite liked it. I was less expensive than some of the other places I looked at on campus.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I thought it was very expensive.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It seemed way more complicated than it actually was. I went smooth, and I had a personal tutor to help me make sure I had done it all the right way.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had a mandatory meeting with a personal tutor, and had to go and be signed in on campus. There probably was more stuff, but I've forgotten what it was.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: A personal tutor could help me.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Unfortunately, a lot of the courses I wanted when I applied for the first time wasn't available, because I had to postpone the stay one semester due to covid. But I still got some interesting courses, and it was very easy to apply and change within the first few weeks.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Talk to your personal tutor if you need help.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked it, but I thought the academic level was a bit lower than in Denmark.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I thought the academic level of the courses was a bit lower than in Denmark. However, the tutorials offered more opportunity to have discussions within the class.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was very different. The lectures and tutorials were only 50 minutes. In UCPH, I'm used to 2-3 hours of lectures and tutorials. However, the tutorial classes in Edinburgh were with less people, which made it more okay to want something explained again or have good discussions with fellow students and teachers. In Edinburgh, there were also tutorial tasks you had to do, which was very involving compared to only reading articles as preparation for class.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Topics in Popular Music 
Scottish Studies 1A: Conceptualising Scotland
What's Up Doc? Introducing Animation Studies

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Topics in Popular Music

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: The apartment was a bit expensive compared to Denmark, when thinking of the condition the apartment was in. Pints and drinks were less expensive than expected. Also, museums were mostly all free.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of societies, so it is easy to be social and find stuff to do.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I joined the film society with film screenings and quiz nights. There was also a whisky society, which I joined a couple of times. A lot of my friends were also a part of the hillwalking society.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
1) Glasgow is a very nice city to visit, and not that far away. 
2) Edinburgh Filmhouse and Cameo are two very cute cinemas showing great films. Also Dominion Cinema in Morningside is a cinema designed like first class on a plane. There are stewardesses and you sit in couches. 
3) King's Theatre and Edinburgh Playhouse are great places to see shows and concerts
4) Go to a rugby game 
5) The Golf Tavern is a great pub with a view over Arthur's Seat 
6) Arthur's Seat 
7) Panda and Sons is a cosy (and expensive) cocktail bar that looks like a barbershop on the outside, but behind a bookshelf is a cosy bar with great drinks 
8) Stockbridge is a cute part of the city with vintage shops and cafes and a great viewpoint 
9) Pub Quizzes (Queen's Arms is a nice pub in new town, and The Southsider has a long hard quiz close to the university) 
10) Morningside has a lot of cute places to have a coffee

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy, because we could speak the language.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join societies.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Can't think of any.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: They are very open and good at small-talking. The culture around the pub and pub quizzes is really nice.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1) If you don't know anyone, then join a society, because you don't necessarily spend a lot of time with people from your class 
2) The academic level in humanities is a bit lower than in Denmark 
3) Edinburgh is a great mix of culture and nature, and with a lot of people from around the world. Most of the Scots are in Glasgow.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Don't think so.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The friendships and the fact that there was so many things to do there.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Don't know.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
